minutes.headline: Committee formed a two-member school start time subcommittee and ratified the teacher contract; budget outlook called grim.
minutes.summary: The calendar advisory committee presented its final report recommending a later start time for grades 6-12 when the new school opens in 2016, plus calendar guidelines. The committee appointed a two-member subcommittee, ratified the integrated agreement with the teachers' association, and moved an early release day to June. The budget hearing was set for April 1, with warnings about state aid and health insurance.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the advisory committee, asked about effects on younger kids, supported keeping costs down, liked whole-week calendar continuity and suggested moving a professional day.

votes.motion: Appoint a school start time subcommittee of two members (Mr. Shapiro and Miss Roka)
Approve the integrated agreement with the teachers' association
Accept the recommended calendar change moving the early release day to June 19

budget_items.what_was_said: The minimum per-student increase has been the old amount; the governor proposed a lower amount, which was called inadequate.
A dramatic increase over what the town manager budgeted is predicted.
Target program designations brought money into the district for field trips and other costs.
The cultural council gave part of the cost and the PTA also helped.
The superintendent said the district cannot afford to spend more on transportation given budget constraints.
A solar spec will be prepared and the cost would come from the owner's contingency.

decisions.decision: School budget hearing to be held April 1 at the televised committee meeting.
Parents to be reminded by phone call the week before the rescheduled half day.
Chair to email the selectmen's office to request a joint reuse committee meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee appointed a two-member subcommittee on school start time, after the calendar advisory committee recommended a later start for grades 6-12.
The committee voted unanimously to approve the integrated agreement with the teachers' association.
The school budget hearing was set for April 1, with warnings about state aid and health insurance costs.
A motion to move the early release day to June 19 was made, but the result is not audible in the recording.
The superintendent said the district cannot afford more spending on transportation for a later start time.

why_it_matters: A later start time for grades 6-12 could change bus schedules and family routines, and the transportation limit means any change has to fit within existing costs.
State aid that was called inadequate and a predicted rise in health insurance costs both put pressure on the school budget that residents will see at the April hearing and later at Town Meeting.
The teacher contract approval sets a labor cost the budget will have to carry.
